Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2) demonstrates bilateral pulmonary nodules and prominent hilar regions, while the corresponding CT scan (Figure 1a) confirms bilateral lung nodules and significant mediastinal/hilar lymphadenopathy. This combination of findings, particularly the symmetric hilar adenopathy with parenchymal nodules, is characteristic of sarcoidosis (often referred to as the "sarcoid galaxy sign" on CT when nodules cluster around lymph nodes), making it the most accurate description among the choices.
